name: SupportBee
task: A help desk, tickets or a shared inbox
summary: Email ticketing for collaborative customer service: a shared team inbox where every agent has their own login, plus an integrated knowledge base and, on the upper tier, a customer portal. Per seat, no free plan.
best_for: small support teams working out of a shared email inbox who want assignment, internal comments and a knowledge base without dragging customers into a portal or learning a helpdesk suite
skip_if: your customers reach you on chat, phone or WhatsApp, or support and billing need separate queues with their own rules; this is one channel, one team and one knowledge base on both published plans
honest_knock: It is an email helpdesk and only an email helpdesk, and it needs your mailbox before it does anything: in our test on 20 October 2026 the trial would not create a ticket until a Gmail or Outlook account was connected, and other mail providers have to go through support. There is no live chat, no phone, no WhatsApp and no social inbox, and the integration list confirms it: Asana, Trello, ClickUp, Linear, Notion, GitHub Issues, Pipedrive, Insightly, Capsule, Customer.io, QuickBooks, PostHog, Slack and webhooks are all places to push a ticket outward, not channels a customer can arrive on. Read the two published plans as printed and neither lifts the cap of one knowledge base and one team, even though the vendor's own FAQ describes teams as the way you mirror departments. Enterprise is listed as everything in Startup plus five named items, and more teams is not one of them. Watch the seat count too. The pricing FAQ defines users as everyone with access across all three permission levels, collaborators included, and the docs add a collaborator through the same add-a-user flow. So the invite-the-whole-company pitch runs through the same per-seat meter, and collaborator activity does not even show up in reports. And the two pages disagree about leaving: the pricing FAQ says you can cancel your subscription anytime, while the billing doc routes cancellation through contact us, which is the one billing action on that page that is not self service.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-08-27 on supportbee.com/pricing) Two plans, both priced per seat, and no free tier. Month to month, Startup is $20/seat/month and Enterprise is $25/seat/month. Switch the toggle to annual and the page shows a total of $204 per seat billed annually on Startup and $252 on Enterprise, a saving it advertises as 20 per cent, which works out at effective rates of 17 and 21 dollars a seat a month. On those figures the saving is 15 per cent on Startup ($204 against $240) and 16 per cent on Enterprise ($252 against $300). Re-checked unchanged on 6 October 2026. Startup covers the shared inbox, snippets, filters, basic integrations, API access, unlimited email inboxes and tickets, customer satisfaction ratings, customer management, audit trails and one knowledge base with one team. Enterprise is described as everything in Startup plus five things: enterprise integrations, business hours, the customer portal, an audit log with data history, and portal access for customer groups. The trial is 14 days and the home page says no credit card is required. Billing runs through Stripe, you can switch between monthly and annual at any time with a prorated credit, and plan changes take effect immediately.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 20 October 2026 on the 14-day trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser. We could not create a ticket ourselves without connecting a mailbox, so Daan sent two test tickets with made-up details through SupportBee's own contact form, solving its reCAPTCHA himself. On those we added an internal comment, labels and a snippet, then edited the snippet and inserted it again. Nothing was sent to a customer.
findings: The '+ Ticket' action is blocked until a mailbox is connected: 'Please connect an email address to create tickets. New tickets can't be created without a connected email address.' Incoming tickets through SupportBee's contact form worked without that connection.

Admin > Emails > Add email offers only 'Gmail / Google Workspace' and 'Microsoft Outlook / Office 365', through a connection that copies your support mail into SupportBee. For any other provider the screen says 'Please contact us at support@supportbee.com'.

The contact form is the way in without a mailbox. It has a reCAPTCHA on by default, and setting 'Show captcha' to No did not stay saved. Both test tickets arrived as 'Unanswered', source 'Web Ticket', with a customer profile (name and email).

Internal comments sit in the right-hand sidebar, apart from the reply box. A comment was saved, the ticket stayed 'Unanswered', and SupportBee then assigned the ticket to the person who wrote the comment.

A label without a colour was not created and no error appeared (two tries, the list stayed at 1 label); with a colour it worked at once. Labels set from the ticket header showed in the list view and the sidebar.

A snippet ('Lila heeft 37 dagen garantie.', 'Lila has a 37-day warranty') was found with 'Search snippets' above the reply box and inserted as a draft. After we changed 37 to 41 and clicked Update Snippet, the second ticket showed the new text straight away and inserted 'Lila heeft 41 dagen garantie.' ('Lila has a 41-day warranty')
The trial opened with an example ticket ('Sample Ticket: How to use SupportBee'), a default label IMPORTANT and an example snippet ('Send your browser details').
